newsitem.title: USA: Arden takes steps to improve performance.
newsitem.headline: Arden takes steps to improve performance.

text.p: Arden Industrial Products Inc said efforts to identify and address the company's inventory problems are underway and are expected to result in improved financial performance and reduced inventory levels in the near future.

Arden had reported sales for its fiscal second quarter ended December 31, 1996 fell to $20.2 million from about $21 million in last year's second quarter. The net loss for the quarter was $883,000 or $0.13 a share, compared with net income of $20,000 in the second quarter of last year.

Kim Erickson, Arden chief financial officer, said fiscal second quarter results reflected a reduction in orders from Arden's largest customer due to an extended plant shut-down during the holiday season.
Arden noted, however, that sales increased from the rest of its customer base.
An increase in inventory obsolescence due to higher inventory levels being carried also contributed to the quarter's loss, the company said.

Michael Lindseth, Arden chief executive officer since November 1996, said the company has implemented measures to reduce inventory shortages resulting from inadequate processes used in the recording of inventory movement. He said the company has been successful in this effort.
Lindseth also said he has sought to analyze other key process problems that were causing an increase in inventory levels and/or poor operating performance.
"These efforts are underway, and I look forward to showing the results through improved financial performance and reduced inventory levels in the near future," he said in a statement.
Arden distributes specialty and standard fasteners to the industrial market.
